content:
maria_p: Quick sync — we need to lock scope for the Optimize Toolkit PRD by EOD Friday. Focus areas: batching configs, prefix/KV caching, and quantization recommendations. Customer asks are getting specific; we should capture requirements + acceptance criteria.

devin_k: +1. Can we prioritize per-route defaults + per-customer overrides? That's the main ask from the platform team and a couple of early customers.

hao_z: Runtime constraints: per-route defaults are fine but we need to validate memory for KV caching when sequence lengths vary. Also quantization guidance must include fallbacks for accuracy-sensitive routes.

sam_j: From GTM: customers want clear rollout gates — e.g., can we phrase launch gates as "no regression >2% on core metrics" and safety net (auto-fallback to fp16 or full model) if perf dips?

jenna_r: For Solutions: include a short checklist that CS can use to triage customer requests (Qs: input distribution, latency SLO, cost target).

maria_p: Agree. Draft acceptance criteria suggestion: 1) API surface: route-level batch/caching/quantization config documented + sample. 2) Default heuristic: autosuggest config based on workload trace. 3) Evaluations: regression tests against canonical prompt set (latency and quality). 4) Rollout policy: canary + auto-fallback. 5) Ops visibility: per-route cost and hit-rate metrics. Thoughts?

devin_k: Make #2 more concrete: autosuggest should propose batch size and KV cache TTL and indicate expected token-savings/cost delta. Also include recommended quantization levels (e.g., int8, q4f16) with expected quality regression numbers.

hao_z: Edge cases to call out: mixed-sequence workloads, streams (server-sent events), and very short-lived high-QPS bursts. Acceptance criteria should include test cases for each.

sam_j: Can we add a non-goal: no fine-tuning/inference-distillation in this phase? That keeps scope tight.

maria_p: Yes, add non-goals. Also we need explicit perf budgets to validate autosuggest — e.g., target p95 latency < 200ms for conversational workloads with batch size <= 8. If that's unrealistic, we flag it.

jenna_r: For CS checklist, propose fields: customer model family, avg seq len, p95 latency SLO, tokens per month, tolerance for quality drop (%). That lets us map to recommendation tables.

devin_k: Quick proto acceptance criteria snippet for the PRD (can paste into doc):

```
Acceptance Criteria (draft):
- API: route config accepts {batching: {enabled,bool, max_batch, window_ms}, caching: {enabled,bool, ttl_ms, prefix_keys}, quant: {levels: ["int8","q4f16","fp16"], default}}
- Autosuggest: given a 24h trace, produce a recommended config + estimated cost delta and expected median latency.
- Eval: regression harness with 3 canonical prompt sets (chat, long-form, code) showing: latency change, token-cost delta, and quality delta (embed/similarity or LM score).
- Rollout: canary threshold rules + auto-fallback to previous model/quant if quality delta > threshold or error-rate spike > X.
- Observability: metrics emitted: batch_size_histogram, cache_hit_rate, quant_failure_count, per_route_cost_per_token.
```

hao_z: Add edge-case tests: 1) 90/10 mix of seq lengths; 2) sudden spike to 10x QPS for 30s; 3) prefix cache key collisions.

sam_j: Product-level launch gates: 1) docs + SDK examples, 2) internal runbook for rollback, 3) two pilot customers onboarded with clear success criteria.

maria_p: Timelines: draft PRD by Wed, RFC with runtime + ml eng feedback by Thu, sign-off Friday. Is that feasible?

devin_k: Wed draft ok, but need runtime to run sims for autosuggest numbers — that'll take ~24h. We can include placeholders but mark as data-needed.

hao_z: I'll run sims starting tomorrow morning. If we can get a representative trace from CustomerA and CustomerB, that speeds it up.

jenna_r: I'll ask CS for two traces and surface any red flags.

ops-bot: Reminder: weekly roadmap sync in #product on Thursday 16:00 UTC.

maria_p: Cool. Next steps: Jenna to fetch traces, Hao to run sims, Devin to mock acceptance snippets in PRD, Sam to craft launch gates. I'll assemble and send the draft PRD link once done. Thanks. :thumbsup:
